title: Execution of the input-reading routine
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $P$ be a register program with $m$ work tapes and $d$ oracle choices, and let its oracle be a function assigning a Boolean answer to each oracle choice and Boolean word. Let $r,s$ be distinct tape indices, let $st$ assign a program state to each reading phase, and let $ex$ assign a program state to each optional Boolean value. Suppose every transition of the ordinary machine from state $st(ph)$ is the specified reading transition with register states mapped by $st$ and terminal states mapped by $ex$, and suppose there are no oracle-call states at any $st(ph)$. If a configuration $c$ has tape $r$ containing the binary representation of $i$, tape $s$ empty, both corresponding heads at position $0$, and input-head position $1$, then some number $T$ of program steps carries the configuration with state $st(eC)$ to the configuration with state $ex$ equal to the $i$th input symbol of $x$ (or no symbol if that index is out of range). At every time $t<T$, the configuration is in the read frame of $c$: only tape $s$'s content may change, the output and other tape contents are preserved, and the heads on tapes $r,s$ lie between $-1$ and the length of the binary representation of $|x|+1$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: A register program $P$ with $m$ tapes and $d$ oracle choices
An oracle function from choices and Boolean words to Boolean answers
Every transition at a state $st(ph)$ agrees with the specified reading transition under $st$ and $ex$
No oracle call is specified at any state $st(ph)$
Tape $r$ of $c$ stores the binary representation of $i$
The heads on tapes $r,s$ in $c$ are at position $0$
